description: Conversion of dwelling into three flats (1 X 1 bed, 1 X 2 bed and 1 X 3 bed); two storey rear extension; alterations and enlargement of roof; landscaping; parking; bin and cycle stores (demolition of existing single storey rear extension and rear outbuilding)(amended description)
decision_conditions: The development hereby permitted shall be begun before the expiration of three years from the date of this permission.

All planting, seeding or turfing comprised in the approved details of landscaping shall be carried out in the first planting and seeding seasons following the occupation of the building(s), or the completion of the development, whichever is the sooner.  Any existing or new trees or shrubs which, within a period of 5 years from the completion of the development, die, are removed, or become seriously damaged or diseased, shall be replaced in the next planting season, with others of a similar size and species, unless the local authority agrees any variation in writing.
The materials to be used in the construction of the external surfaces of the extension hereby permitted shall match those used in the existing building.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans and documents: A101; A102; A103; A104; A105; A106; A107; A108; A109; A110; A111; A112; A113; A114; A115; Daylight and Sunlight Report (Within Development); 107 GORDON AVENUE, HA7 3QY DESIGN AND ACCESS STATEMENT; 10550 - 107 Gordon Avenue - FRA&SuDS Strategy-2605-15nv; 11550 – 107 Gordon Avenue – PEA & BNG – 2605-13ks; 11550 – 107 Gordon Avenue – Statutory BNG Metric – 2605-11ks.

The window(s) and doors in the eastern and western (ground floor only)  elevation(s) of the proposed development shall:
(a) be of purpose-made obscure glass,
(b) be permanently fixed closed below a height of 1.7m above finished floor level,
and shall thereafter be retained in that form.

<p>No site works or development shall commence until details of the levels of the extension and existing building, road(s) and footpath(s) in relation to the adjoining land and highway(s), and any other changes proposed in the levels of the site, have been submitted to, and approved by, the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the approved details, the development hereby permitted shall not commence until there has been a scheme of hard and soft landscape works for the site submitted to, and approved by the Local Planning Authority. Soft landscape works shall include:</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>i.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>planting plans (at a scale not less than 1:100),&nbsp;</p><p>ii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>schedules of plants, noting species, plant sizes, plant container sizes (all at time of planting) and&nbsp;</p><p>iii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>proposed numbers / densities.&nbsp;</p><p>iv.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>Written specification of planting and cultivation works to be undertaken, and</p><p>v.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>A landscape implementation programme with proposed timing / dates for the works.</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>Hard landscape works shall include:&nbsp;</p><p><br></p><p>vi.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>details of boundary treatments (materials, scale of boundary, location) and gates&nbsp;</p><p>vii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>privacy screening/boundary treatment to prevent overlooking to the single bedroom window in the ground floor of flat A</p><p>viii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>details of hard surfacing materials to be used in the landscaping of the site.&nbsp;</p><p><br></p><p>The development will be undertaken in accordance with the approved details and thereafter retained.</p>

<p>No development shall take place (including vegetation/site clearance) until a Precautionary Working Method Statement (PWMS) for nesting birds has been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The PWMS should include, but may not be limited to;</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>i.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>A toolbox talk covering the ecology of and legislation which protects species which may be present on site, to be delivered to construction personnel by the ECoW;</p><p>ii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>A plan showing areas of sensitivity and exclusion zones;</p><p>iii.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>Details of where and how waste and/or construction materials will be stored;</p><p>iv.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>Details of which construction tasks pose a risk to protected species, and will therefore be supervised by the ECoW;</p><p>v.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>Measures for supervised vegetation clearance (e.g., phased, directional cut);</p><p>vi.<span style="white-space:pre">	</span>Procedures to be followed if a protected species is discovered.</p><p>&nbsp;</p><p>The approved PWMS shall be implemented in full according to the specified timescales, unless otherwise agreed in writing by the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of construction (other than demolition works), a scale, colour plan of biodiversity enhancements on the site, to include the number, specification, and location of enhancements such as bat boxes, hedgehog highways, and bird boxes, shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Thereafter, the biodiversity enhancement measures shall be carried out and retained in accordance with the approved details.</p>

<p>Prior to the commencement of works (other than demolition) hereby approved, a Fire Safety Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The statement shall include details of the following:</p><p><br></p><p>a) identify suitably positioned unobstructed outside space:</p><p>i) for fire appliances to be positioned on</p><p>ii) appropriate for use as an evacuation assembly point</p><p>b) is designed to incorporate appropriate features which reduce the risk to life and the risk of serious injury in the event of a fire; including appropriate fire alarm systems and passive and active fire safety measures</p><p>c) is constructed in an appropriate way to minimise the risk of fire spread</p><p>d) provide suitable and convenient means of escape, and associated evacuation strategy for all building users</p><p>e) develop a robust management strategy for evacuation which is to be periodically updated and published (details of how often this management strategy is to be reviewed and published to be included), and which all building users can have confidence in</p><p>f) provide suitable access and equipment for firefighting which is appropriate for the size and use of the development. The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.</p><p><br></p><p>The development shall be operated in accordance with the approved details in perpetuity.</p>

<p>Prior to commencement of development, a Construction Logistics Plan and Method Statement shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority in accordance with the format and guidance provided by Transport for London – www.tfl.gov.uk. The Detailed Construction Logistics Plan shall provide for:</p><p><br></p><p>a) Parking of vehicles of site operatives/visitors;</p><p>b) HGV access to site – loading and unloading of plant and materials;</p><p>c) Number of HGV’s anticipated;</p><p>d) Storage of plant and materials used in constructing the development;</p><p>e) Programme of work and phasing;</p><p>f) Site layout plan;</p><p>g) Highway condition (before, during, after);</p><p>h) Measures to control dust and dirt during construction;</p><p>i) A scheme for recycling/disposing of waste resulting from demolition and construction works; and</p><p>j) details showing the frontage/ the boundary of the site enclosed by site hording to a minimum height of 2 metres.</p><p><br></p><p>The development shall be carried out in accordance with the approved Detailed Construction Logistics Plan and Method Statement, or any amendment or variation to it as may be agreed in writing by the local planning authority.</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the approved details and prior to the commencement of works of the development hereby permitted, full details of permeable paving shall be submitted to, and approved in writing, by the local planning authority. The development shall be carried out in accordance with these approved details and shall thereafter be retained.</p>

<p>Notwithstanding the approved plans and prior to the first occupation of the development hereby permitted full details of bin stores and enclosures should be submitted to and approved writing by the Local Planning Authority. The refuse bins shall be stored at all times, other than on collection days, in the designated refuse storages as approved and retained thereafter.</p>

<p>Prior to the first occupation of the development, evidence of Secured by Design Certification shall be submitted to the local planning authority to be agreed in writing, or justification shall be submitted where the accreditation requirements cannot be met. Secure by design measures shall be implemented and the development shall be retained in accordance with the approved details.&nbsp;</p>

<p>The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until details of all external lighting to be provided within the site have been submitted to and approved in writing by the local planning authority. The details shall include lighting specifications, manufacturer information, elevations, light spillage and lighting levels. The external lighting shall be implemented in accordance with the approved details prior to first occupation of the development and shall be retained thereafter.</p>

<p>The cycle storage shall be made available in accordance with the details as shown on Drawing No. A107 prior to the first occupation of the development hereby approved and shall be retained thereafter.</p>
